recipes.name: Cordon Bleu Chicken Rolls
ingredients_raw: 4 slices Swiss cheese, cut into 1 inch pieces
1 (10.75 ounce) can condensed cream of chicken soup

steps.text: Gather all ingredients and preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C). Lightly grease a 9x13-inch baking dish.
Make the chicken rolls: Place each chicken breast half between sheets of plastic wrap and pound with a meat mallet to about 1/8 inch thickness.

Place a piece of cheese on each ham slice and sprinkle lightly with thyme and salt and pepper to taste. Roll up seasoned ham and cheese jellyroll-style, then roll each chicken breast with ham and cheese inside. Tuck in ends and fasten with toothpicks.

Place melted butter in a small bowl and place cereal crumbs in a shallow dish or bowl. Dip each chicken roll in butter, then roll in crumbs, turning to coat thoroughly. Place coated rolls in the prepared baking dish.
Bake in the preheated oven until chicken is golden brown and juices run clear, about 40 minutes.
While the chicken is cooking, prepare the cordon bleu sauce: Mix together condensed soup, sour cream, and lemon juice in a small saucepan. Heat over low heat, stirring occasionally, until combined.
Serve sauce hot over chicken rolls. Enjoy!

raw_recipe.headline: Cordon Bleu Chicken Rolls
raw_recipe.description: Breaded chicken stuffed with ham and cheese tastes extraordinary. This cordon bleu chicken recipe is the best with an easy cream sauce to boot.

video.description: There’s no need to be intimidated by Chicken Cordon Bleu with these simple steps for creating the classic Blue Ribbon chicken rolls! Pound chicken breasts to tenderize them, then place ham, Swiss cheese and salt and pepper inside, roll up “jelly roll style,” and fasten with toothpicks. Dip each roll in butter and cornflake crumbs and bake. Create a quick gravy of cream of mushroom soup, sour cream and lemon juice, and serve rolls sliced atop a bed of the gravy with a side veggie or pasta and enjoy a great meal.

review.reviewBody:
Updated review: I made this recipe again tonight. This time I used a combination of crushed corn flakes and italian bread crumbs. I again used munster cheese instead of swiss. I decided to try the gravy and it was good, but I don't think it's necessary as the chicken tastes great alone.

Original review: My husband says this is the best new recipe that I've ever made, and he's hard to please. 

I did things slightly different for personal preferences. First of all, I used Italian bread crumbs instead of Corn Flake crumbs because that's all I had in the house. I used munster cheese instead of swiss becuase neither of us like Swiss. And I didn't make the gravy, because my husband isn't a gravy person. 

These were so simple to make, took little time and turned out wonderfully. The first time I made this it came out too dry, so I adjusted my cooking temperature the next time to 350, for 30 minutes, and it worked fine. I will definately make this again!
My one suggestion is to use dry spaghetti instead of toothpicks. They cook right along with the roll and you don't have to go looking for toothpicks to remove.

With a little altering, these came out wonderful and were delicious! I took the advice of another reviewer and spread a little mayonnaise on the breasts before inserting the ham and cheese "fingers" and rolling them up, securing them with some wooden toothpicks that had been soaked in water for a bit. I also used panko bread crumbs seasoned with a little of Emeril's BAM, parley flakes, salt and pepper because I didn't have any cornflakes. The sauce was a nice complement to the chicken. I did, however, need to thin it a bit with water to get it to the preferred consistency. I served this with mushroom wild rice and baby Brussels sprouts in a butter sauce. Definitely an elegant and memorable meal. I'll be making this one again.

My kids love this recipe! I slice the chicken in half - like I'm fileting it. That way I start with a thinner piece and then I pound it as flat as I need too. After stuffing it, I also roll it in egg whites and then a combination of panko bread crumbs, basil and Parmesan cheese and spray with Pam before baking, which gives it a nice crunch. No need for toothpicks, as they burn and are a pain to remove. I cook at 425 for around 30 minutes - really tasty! The sauce is amazing :)

400 degrees for 45 min. Use 1/4-1/3 cup of breadcrumbs and same amount of crushed cereal Honey Bunches of Oats. Use 1-2 tbsp of melted butter with a little egg whites. Add to bottom of red pan about 1/3 cup of white wine mixed with a little chicken bouillon. Add salt, pepper, and thyme to chicken.

This was excellent. We had a friend coming over who can’t eat gluten so this was great because it uses cornflakes instead of panko/breadcrumbs. I used Jarlsberg Swiss cheese and yes, it did leak out a bit because I wasn’t adept enough to get all the ends tucked in tight, but it still tasted great. Will definitely make again even when gluten isn’t a factor.

Absolutely loved it! Here was my variation that I think nailed it! First I used Italian bread crumbs. But the sauce is where I leveled up. I use half as much soup as was suggested, a little more sour cream than was suggested... More lemon than what suggested I included lemon zest... But the real kicker was I also added half a cup of Dijon mustard. Everyone loved every bit of it!

I used what I had on hand - american cheese and mozzarella cheese (some with one, some with the other) , Special K for the cereal, and cream of asparagus soup instead of cream of chicken. It was a hit! My daughter didn't care for the sauce but the rest of us loved it. I may add a little spiced bread crumbs or just some herbs to the coating to add some more flavor. And I should've read previous reviews because the cheese ran out the sides on me . Now I know for next time - and there will definitely be a next time!

I kicked up the sauce by adding garlic salt and pepper, and thinned it out with a little half and half- it turned out very smooth and flavorful. I didn't have thyme, so I substituted sage and it tasted great. Should have flattened out the chicken a little more, or bought bigger chicken breasts because it was tricky to get the parcel completely sealed.

It was great, I baked it for 50 min and instead of Swiss cheese I used a mix of mozzarella and cheddar. I also ended up mixing mayonnaise and Parmesan into the butter for the crust, and finishing it off with bread crumbs.
I made this recipe but I did not use corn flakes. I used crushed organic butter-style golden round crackers. It was delicious!!!!

Fast, easy and tasty. Used black forest ham and as others I used Panko bread crumbs. For the sauce I cheated and used Knorr hollandaise sauce mix. Served with mashed potatoes but think next time would use rice.

This was delicious - the only minor modifications were using plain breadcrumbs seasoned with salt and pepper (only bc I forgot to buy the cornflakes), using slightly more cheese, adding a little mayo to the butter, and including a touch of mustard and smoked paprika to the sauce. I was concerned it might be a little dry, but nope. Moist and cooked perfectly right at 40 minutes total! The family raved about it!!
Excellent just as presented. I used the quick method and it provided a lot of flavor.

This is a great dish without too much work. I made a couple of changes to suit my preference. I Substituted panko bread crumbs for corn flakes and doubled up the cheese amount. Lastly, I added smoked paprika and red chili flakes to the sauce. I am making again tonight!
Haven't tried it yet but wanted to thank you.
So easy, yummy and looks like you spent ages doing it! I use Japanese breadcrumbs (Panko) and they work a treat.
I’m making this tonight and wonder if I can use unsalted crackers instead of any other breading. Do I need to adjust cook time or temperature doing that?
It tasted great. I did not have cereal so I used a chicken batter mix. It turned out, its a spicy mix but it was good.

The recipe is interesting and feels good in the preparation and the use of ingredients. Thank you very much for submitting. I rolled up the chicken like a jelly roll with ham and cheese slices laid out on the pounded chicken, maybe next time I'll make a center roll of ham and cheese. I read the sauce and crumb comments. Every cook and kitchen has their preferences, right? This is French Country cooking, not Haute Cuisine.
